text:
Tel Maridun’s latest excavation was led by Prof. Ansel Okafor, the University of Veyra said Tuesday. The six-week dig in the southern trench exposed 14 sealed rooms and 37 catalogued tablets, with initial conservation costs pegged at 1.8 million dalens. Okafor’s team of 26 researchers and technicians also recovered bronze fittings and two intact storage jars, now heading to the Maridun Regional Archive for analysis.

The find matters for the heritage sector because it strengthens the case for pre-sale survey work before infrastructure projects in the basin. Several contractors operating nearby have already asked for updated ground-risk assessments, and insurers are expected to tighten archaeological contingency pricing next quarter.
